page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head at the top, page number at the top left. A marginal reference ("Philip. 2.17.") stands in the left margin beside the line "& desideret". Catchword at the lower right.

main_text.p: us, hi enim soli effugiunt castigationem illam paternam, cujus omnes hæredes Dei & cohæredes Christi, hoc aut illo modo participes fieri testatur Apostolus; quoniam hæc militiæ Christianæ lex lata est, ne quis coronetur, nisi qui legitimè certaverit. Certandum itaque cum sit, eò nos conferamus ubi minimo cum periculo, maximâ cum certitudine præmium amplissimum comparari potest. Procedamus cum Domino Christo, ex superbis corruptæ iam Hierosolymæ mœnis: crucem ejus ferentes ad horrida mortuorum loca properemus, ut sitiat anima nostra Dominum, Philip. 2.17.& desideret eum caro nostra in terra deserti & sitibunda, in qua non est aqua verbi divini, ut ibi sacrificia Deo per Christum grata, offeramus. Ne fugiamus Baptismum, quo Dominus gloriæ pro peccatis nostris baptisatus fuit; læ-temur potius & exultemus, si pro mortuis baptisari detur: si baptisemur baptismo mortis & afflictionis pro incredulis, qui mortui in peccato, sub caligine & umbra mortis detenti, ad conspectam lucem vitæ, quam hactenus ignorarunt, avidè confluxuri sunt. Nemo in hac semente grani sui iacturam metuat,

page.notes: The marginal reference "Philip. 2.17." is printed in the left margin; its letters are slightly blurred, so the chapter and verse numbers are read with some care. "Hierosolymæ" is printed with a long-s form that could also be read as "Hierofolymæ"; the reading given follows the usual spelling. The word "læ-" is hyphenated at the line end and is kept as printed. The catchword "metuat," is at the lower right and is kept with its comma.
